Create a convincing tactile hand-worked earthen daub wall from a modest 1835 island rancho: muted warm gray-brown clay, tiny straw fibers embedded in plaster, uneven hand-smoothed shallow ridges, fine drying cracks. A few small irregular losses expose narrow weathered split cane woven horizontally around thin vertical stakes beneath the earth; exposed areas total no more than 12 percent of area. Cane is fibrous rounded strips, never bricks or masonry. Color range restrained, mostly midtone dusty taupe ochre; no orange cast. Small detail visible at close camera distance, medium-scale variation quiet. Flat diffuse shadowless lighting suitable for albedo; no directional light, ambient occlusion, specular highlights, cast shadows, perspective, border, labels or text. Edges must tile seamlessly left-right and top-bottom; no central motif. Deliver one square color texture only, not a material preview or contact sheet.
